instrument: Virginia Data Center Accountability Framework (proposed; 2027 General Assembly legislative agenda)
section: Bolster our Clean Energy Economy & Grid Reliability
summary: Proposes to limit electricity data centers generate from on-site or behind-the-meter natural gas, prioritize grid access for facilities investing in clean energy, and make it easier to bring their own clean power by reforming utility charges that discourage it; also proposes ride-through-type standards against sudden demand changes.
text: Protect grid reliability by requiring data centers to meet standards that prevent sudden changes in their electricity demand from destabilizing the grid; Limit the amount of electricity data centers can generate from on-site natural gas or behind-the-meter gas generation; Accelerate clean energy deployment by prioritizing grid access for facilities that invest in clean energy, further reduce backup generator emissions, and further limit on-site natural gas generation; Make it easier for data centers to bring their own clean power, including by reforming utility charges that discourage investment in clean energy

source.citation: Office of the Governor of Virginia, news release, Governor Spanberger Unveils Nation's Most Comprehensive & Aggressive Data Center Accountability Standards, Signs Executive Order to Immediately Put Into Action, September 18, 2026

notes: Draws the bring-your-own-power line at fuel: gas limited, clean encouraged. Compare Oregon DCAC Preliminary Learnings (BYONCE, September 2026) and Evolved Energy Research on the gas-price channel (September 17, 2026).
confidence_note: Read in original from the Governor's release, which lists the Framework's contents. The Framework document itself was not opened (link behind a redirect). Framework items are proposals for the 2027 General Assembly and are NOT in force except where Executive Order 22 implements them; see the us-va-state EO 22 entries.
